record.provider: Maven Central (Sonatype Central Portal / Central Publisher)

free_tier.stated: No total storage quota, but as of 2026 a monthly publishing quota per organization on three metrics, with thresholds set at the ~90th percentile: 1,167 files / 78 MB release size / 7 releases per month at p90, rising to 17,724 / 1,808 MB / 50 at p99. The 1 GB archive upload limit is the per-request cap. Commercial-nature artefacts require the paid Publisher Pro tier from Oct 1 2026 regardless of volume.

retention.stated: 30-day grace period on breach, then new releases refused

egress.terms: Free and unmetered, Cloudflare-fronted. Probe: repo1.maven.org jar GET -> 200, Server: cloudflare, CF-RAY present, no auth.

record.tooling: Upload via Central Portal archive upload (zip/tar.gz up to 1 GB following Maven repo layout) or the maven-deploy-plugin; download via plain GET on repo1.maven.org/maven2/<group>/<artifact>/<version>/<file>. Every Java build tool is a client. No rclone backend.
record.chaining: Weakest chain in the field because the new quota is per organization per month: 78 MB/month at the p90 threshold means a new org yields ~78 MB/month of headroom. Unlimited free orgs would multiply it, but each org requires a verified namespace and a GPG-signed artefact chain, so the setup cost per GB is the worst here.
record.limits_note: 1 GB per upload archive. Monthly per-org: file count, total release size, release count (see table). 30-day grace period on breach, then new releases refused. Signed artefacts only; namespace ownership must be proven. Published artefacts remain downloadable forever ('Already-published artifacts are never affected').
record.reliability_note: Data never vanishes (already-published artefacts are explicitly exempt from any enforcement). The failure mode is publishing stopping after the grace period. A bulk writer will hit the release-size threshold in the first month and be blocked. This quota regime is new (2026) and the page says thresholds 'may be adjusted as we learn'.

evidence.proved: monthly thresholds table ('90th | 1,167 | 78 | 7' ... card.summary: Free, self-hosted, no storage quota: 'There is no cost to use Sonatype Nexus Repository Community Edition'; the feature matrix marks 'Unlimited Nexus Reposit...

free_tier.stated: Free, self-hosted, no storage quota: 'There is no cost to use Sonatype Nexus Repository Community Edition'; the feature matrix marks 'Unlimited Nexus Repository Deployments' as included. Storage is your blob store, so the ceiling is your disk.

egress.terms: Free by construction (self-hosted). Serve through Cloudflare or your own CDN at your own cost.

record.interface_detail: rest (Nexus REST API v1), native protocols for maven/npm/pypi/nuget/docker/raw/helm/apt/yum, WebDAV-ish raw repos
record.tooling: `curl -u` against `/service/rest/v1/components`, `mvn deploy`, `npm publish`, `twine upload`, `docker push`; a well-documented REST API for scripting.
record.chaining: Same as any self-hosted manager: unlimited instances × your disk. The version that matters for this brief is that nothing in Nexus meters bytes, so a single instance on a cheap VPS with a big volume gives unbounded logical storage. But you buy the volume.
record.limits_note: No published byte limit, but Sonatype positions CE as 'a small team solution ... with modest usage' and tells larger users to buy Pro. Pro-only features include cloud blob stores (S3/Azure/GCS), so CE is stuck on local disk. Raw repositories can hold arbitrary files but there is no public anonymous sharing story as clean as Cloudsmith's.
record.reliability_note: Mature and stable; the only 'limit' is a licensing/positioning nudge, not a technical cut-off. Data does not vanish.

evidence.proved: read live: 'There is no cost to use Sonatype Nexus Repository Community Edition. You can get started for free, no credit card is required'; 'designed to be a small team solution that can be used for free with modest usage'
